zh.name: Mandarin
zh.intro: Four tones and a neutral tone. The G2P gives each character its dictionary reading, so tone sandhi is not applied (a 3rd tone before another 3rd tone is still 214, though it is said as 35) and particles may carry their full tone.

214.name: Tone 3, dipping
214.desc: ǎ; shǎngshēng 上声. Before another syllable it is often only low (21).

3.name: Neutral tone
3.desc: qīngshēng 轻声: short and unstressed; its pitch follows the tone before it
examples: n a35 n t s ɯ3

5.name: (rare)
5.desc: only in spelled-out letters and foreign words
examples: ɛ55 n p j ɑ ʊ55 ɛ5 s

yue.name: Cantonese
yue.intro: Six tones, numbered 1–6 in Jyutping. Level tones are written with one digit. The checked (entering) tones of syllables ending in p, t, k share the number of the level tone at the same height.

5.name: Tone 1, high level
examples: f ɔ5 ŋ s ɪ5 k

35.name: Tone 2, high rising
examples: j ɪ35 ŋ h œ35 ŋ

3.name: Tone 3, mid level
examples: s ɐ i3 k a i3
k w ɔ3 k k a5

21.name: Tone 4, low falling
examples: s ɪ21 ŋ w ɐ i21
p ɐ5 t tʰ ʊ21 ŋ

2.name: Tone 6, low level
examples: t ʊ2 ŋ m ɐ2 t
w u2 t t ʊ2 ŋ

vi.name: Vietnamese (Northern)
vi.intro: Six tones, shown by the accent marks of the spelling. Sắc is split in two: syllables ending in p, t, c, ch take a short high rise (45). Counts are from Northern Vietnamese (vi); vi-c and vi-s may number some tones differently.

45.name: sắc, high rising (checked)
45.desc: acute on a syllable ending in p, t, c, ch: các, nhất

35.name: ngã, broken rising
35.desc: tilde: ã; often with a glottal break in the middle

3.name: (rare)
examples: m a r t ɛ3 l i33
ă3 w k l a33 n d

th.name: Thai
th.intro: Five tones. The tone of a syllable follows from its consonant class, vowel length, ending and tone mark; the G2P works it out.

114.name: rising tone
114.desc: siang chattawa: starts low, then rises
